guard: a mutation's named cell must be able to observe the file the mutation edits, so an entry cannot edit an end-to-end guard while naming a cell no edit to that file could ever redden
why: `expectRed` is machine-checked to redden and `cell` is not checked against behaviour at all, so an entry can edit an end-to-end guard, name a parser-only cell, and grade a clean KILLED off the collateral red. WRONG-RED cannot fire on it: that verdict exists for the named assertion NOT reddening, never for it reddening for an unrelated reason. PR #1521 shipped two such entries.

The mutations fall into two halves. The first three remove the refusal, the relation it rests on, and the analysis that makes the relation decidable; each must redden the cell that names the refusal. The last four widen the analysis so a self-fed cell reads as observing something, and they matter more than the first three: a check that accepts everything is indistinguishable in every log from one that is working, which is the defect this whole file is about.

NOT ASSERTED, and recorded rather than implied: that the named cell observes the RIGHT thing. Two end-to-end cells driving the same binary through different paths both carry a launch witness, so naming either one passes. That is the larger half of the class and it stays open, because deciding it needs the semantics of the guard rather than the reachability of the suite. No mutation here claims otherwise.

NO top-level `completionMarker`. This suite reports every cell and then exits non-zero, so its summary line prints on a red run too - but its EXPECTED_CELLS line does not, and pointing a marker at a line a red run may not reach turns a genuine kill INCONCLUSIVE.
